blocks.x: Applied AI & GenAI inside Banking & Financial Services: what the sector's controls demand, what we build on the platform rails, and the outcomes written into the engagement.

In Banking & Financial Services, applied ai & generative ai at dataq soft covers the full lifecycle of enterprise intelligence: strategy and value mapping, platform build-out, model adaptation, retrieval architectures, multimodal systems, and the governance fabric that keeps every model auditable. That is the baseline pattern; the differentiator is what it connects to: enterprise ai strategy & roadmapping, generative ai platform engineering, llm fine-tuning & model operations — delivered on Dataq Compass and Dataq Forge and Dataq Nexus with the sector's regulatory posture built in.

items: GenAI stuck between pilot and policy

Generative assistants for credit memos, research summaries and client drafts stall in model-risk review because guardrails, provenance and audit trails were not designed in. Shadow AI fills the gap, creating exactly the exposure the review was meant to prevent.
Service deflection without resolution
Chatbots deflect contact volume but not intent; repeat contact within seven days rises while CSAT falls. Front-line teams inherit escalations stripped of context.
KYC and periodic-review backlog

Customer due diligence refresh cycles lag behind actual risk changes; files queue for weeks in review pools while remediation backlogs grow. Manual file assembly across registries, screening tools and core systems consumes analyst hours that produce no judgment.

blocks.x: Two regimes anchor the control design here: GDPR / privacy regimes and DORA (EU). ICT risk, incident reporting, resilience testing and third-party oversight obligations with supervisory scrutiny. Evidence for both is generated by the delivery itself — control tests, replay trails and documentation are artifacts of the program, not a reconstruction project.

Programs run on the fixed rhythm below, chosen so progress is legible from week one. Weeks 1–2 are measurement only: we lock the current metric with your team and both sides sign it before a line of build starts. Weeks 3–8 deliver a bounded pilot — one decision path, one workflow, one plant or one portfolio — with a named control owner on your side. Weeks 9–12 turn what worked into runbooks, monitoring and enablement, then report the measured delta against the baseline. A missed gate means a documented stop-or-redirect decision, not a quiet extension.
